name: Hotel Japfu Restaurant
why_it_matters: Government-run hotel restaurant on P.R. Hill, operating since 1988 under the Nagaland tourism department. Multi-cuisine kitchen (Indian, Chinese, Naga) — useful as a one-stop dining option for traveling families that want a Naga thali alongside familiar Indian food. Long-stayer on every Kohima foodie roundup.
insider_tip: Naga thali is the headline order — at government rates, this is the cheapest sit-down Naga thali in town. The hotel itself is dated, but the kitchen is dependable. Wide vegetarian options.

name: Café Samsara (Niraamaya Retreats Aradura)
why_it_matters: All-day dining inside Niraamaya Retreats Aradura — Kohima's only luxury wellness resort, built into the Aradura ridge. The Café Samsara kitchen runs authentic Naga (smoked pork-bamboo, axone) alongside continental and Asian; halal-certified for Chinese, Nepalese and European cuisines. The most consistent fine-dining option in Kohima for non-residents who book in advance.
insider_tip: Non-residents can dine here but call ahead — the kitchen runs on resort cadence. Order the smoked pork with bamboo shoot (the property's signature) plus one continental plate; the European section is genuinely competent, unlike most Kohima 'continental' menus.
signature_address: P/C 55, New Ministers Hill, Aradura, Kohima 797001

name: De Oriental Grand Restaurant
why_it_matters: Hotel restaurant inside De Oriental Grand on High School Road — one of the central Kohima hotels with a sit-down dining room serving Naga ethnic cuisine alongside Indian and Chinese. 30 guest rooms above; the kitchen runs all day for hotel residents and walk-ins.
insider_tip: Useful if you're staying anywhere on High School Road or near Themezie — saves the walk to Jail Colony. Ask the staff which Naga dishes are running fresh that day; the menu rotates with the kitchen's smoking schedule.
